top_signal.title: Is community/forum software still a good SaaS business to build?
top_signal.summary: I've spent close to 20 years building and running online communities.   Over that time, I've seen firsthand how valuable a good community can be for a business: customer conversations, peer support, feedback, retention, word of mouth, and a growing body of useful content.   That background is what led me to build a SaaS in 2024: a white-label community/forum platform for businesses.   I also liked the market for a few reasons:     The category is already proven. There are established companies making serious revenue from community/forum software.   Businesses already run communities across forums, Slack, Discord, Facebook Groups, etc.   I believe useful human conversations will become more valuable as the web fills with AI-generated content.   One of our product bets is that public community content should also help businesses get discovered through Google and AI search, rather than community being purely a retention/engagement tool.     The business is profitable today, and we have a small number of customers who genuinely like the product.   But there's one problem:    Finding new customers is much harder than I expected.    That has made me question something more fundamental than our marketing.    Is community/forum software actually a good business to be in today?    Do enough businesses genuinely care about owning a customer community to pay for dedicated software?   Or is community one of those things companies like the idea of, but rarely consider important enough to
